title: This Bird Eats Bees All Day and Strips Their Stingers First
subject: bee-eater

scenes.text: This bird lives on bees. How does it not get stung?
Bees and wasps make up about seventy percent of a bee-eater's diet on average.
It catches one in the air, then knocks its head against a branch to stun it.
Then it rubs the bee's tail along the branch, stripping off the stinger and venom sac.
Some rub with their eyes shut. A captive juvenile did it by instinct, but was stung at first.
Only then does it swallow. Not one sting left. Just a snack.

description:
Bee-eaters get about seventy percent of their diet from bees and wasps on average.
They stun each insect, rub off the stinger and venom sac on a branch, then swallow it.
Which animal has the strangest diet you know?
first_comment: Would you eat a bee if you could remove the stinger? What other animal eats something dangerous and gets away with it?
